specAnchors.text: understand the roles of oestrogen and testosterone in the development of secondary sexual characteristics

primer.text: Puberty rewires a body in a few years, and the foreman on that building site is a single hormone per sex. This note assigns the changes to their hormones — oestrogen driving the female set, testosterone the male set — and explains which changes both sexes share and why emotions run high while the hormones climb.

modules.title: Hormones Behind the Changes of Puberty
modules.opening: Secondary sexual characteristics are the changes that appear during puberty, switched on by hormones: oestrogen builds the female pattern while testosterone builds the male pattern, and both hormones rise high enough to stir emotional changes too.
keyPoints: Secondary sexual characteristics are the body changes that puberty brings.
Their development is controlled by hormones released at puberty.
Oestrogen produces the female characteristics, such as breast development and wider hips.
Testosterone produces the male characteristics, such as a breaking voice and developing muscles.
Both sexes grow body hair and sexual organs, and hormones drive emotional changes.

low.restatement: At puberty one hormone per sex switches on the adult body plan: oestrogen for female features, testosterone for male features.
low.analogy: Two builders following two different house plans from the same street of cells.
low.examPointer: Name the hormone with each list of changes — the spec asks for the roles of both.

medium.restatement: The changes are secondary because the reproductive machinery already exists; the hormones enlarge and repurpose it, adding visible markers of sexual maturity and, through their action on the brain, shifts in mood and interest in sex.
medium.analogy: A software update that reveals features the hardware carried all along.
medium.examPointer: Include the shared changes and the emotional ones — lists that stop at breasts and voices drop marks.

glossary.definition: The body changes that develop during puberty under hormone control.
The female sex hormone that drives female secondary sexual characteristics.
The male sex hormone that drives male secondary sexual characteristics.
The stage of development in which secondary sexual characteristics appear.
